clinicalPearls: SPG39 is an autosomal recessive complicated HSP caused by variants in PNPLA6, which encodes neuropathy target esterase (NTE).
Distal amyotrophy and wasting affecting the hands and feet accompany the spastic paraparesis, a distal-wasting picture that overlaps clinically with Troyer syndrome.
Onset is typically in childhood with slow progression over subsequent years.

PNPLA6 underlies an allelic spectrum that includes Gordon Holmes syndrome, Boucher-Neuhauser syndrome, Oliver-McFarlane syndrome and Laurence-Moon syndrome, so hypogonadism, ataxia and retinal disease may coexist.
Neuropathy target esterase is the historical molecular target of organophosphate-induced delayed neuropathy, linking this inherited disorder to a classical toxicological pathway.
Screening for hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism and chorioretinal dystrophy can uncover the wider syndrome even when the initial presentation looks like isolated distal-wasting HSP.
Cerebellar atrophy on imaging should prompt consideration of the ataxic end of the PNPLA6 spectrum.
The combination of pyramidal signs with distal wasting in the upper and lower limbs is a useful clinical signature.
reference.pathophysiology: SPG39 is caused by biallelic variants in PNPLA6, which encodes neuropathy target esterase (NTE), a membrane-bound lysophospholipase anchored in the endoplasmic reticulum. NTE deacylates phosphatidylcholine and its lyso derivative, regulating the turnover and homeostasis of glycerophospholipids that maintain neuronal membrane integrity. Loss of esterase activity disturbs this lipid balance, allowing accumulation of lysophosphatidylcholine and disrupting membrane dynamics in metabolically demanding, long axons; the corticospinal tracts and distal peripheral motor axons are particularly affected, producing spastic paraparesis with distal amyotrophy. The same enzyme is expressed in the hypothalamic-pituitary axis and the retina, which explains why more extensive loss of function produces the allelic phenotypes of hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism, cerebellar ataxia and chorioretinal degeneration. NTE is also the well-recognised target inhibited in organophosphate-induced delayed neuropathy.
additionalDifferentials: Troyer syndrome (SPG20/spartin), which also features distal amyotrophy with spasticity
SPG7 (paraplegin) complicated HSP with cerebellar and other features
Boucher-Neuhauser and Gordon Holmes syndromes (allelic PNPLA6 disorders)
Distal hereditary motor neuropathies where wasting dominates
Other complicated HSP subtypes presenting with amyotrophy or ataxia
additionalInvestigations: Nerve conduction studies and electromyography for a distal motor axonal process
MRI of the brain looking for cerebellar atrophy
Endocrine assessment for hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism using gonadotrophins and sex steroids
Ophthalmological evaluation with electroretinography for chorioretinal dystrophy
Assessment of distal muscle bulk and power in hands and feet
redFlags: Failure of pubertal development or other features of hypogonadism
Progressive visual loss suggesting chorioretinal degeneration
Rapidly advancing distal weakness and wasting
reference.prognosis: SPG39 typically follows a slowly progressive course with disability accumulating from combined spasticity and distal wasting; when the wider PNPLA6 spectrum is present, the endocrine, cerebellar and retinal features add substantially to long-term morbidity.
pitfalls: Overlooking the endocrine and retinal features of the allelic PNPLA6 spectrum and missing a unifying diagnosis
Mistaking the distal wasting for a distal hereditary motor neuropathy or Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease
Failing to recognise autosomal recessive inheritance in small families
Confusing the distal-wasting phenotype with Troyer syndrome without genetic confirmation

management: Symptomatic antispasticity therapy with baclofen or tizanidine, and botulinum toxin for focal lower-limb spasticity
Physiotherapy and occupational therapy addressing combined spasticity and distal amyotrophy, with orthoses and adaptive aids for hand and foot weakness
Endocrine management of hypogonadotrophic hypogonadism, including sex-hormone replacement where the wider PNPLA6 spectrum such as Gordon Holmes or Boucher-Neuhauser syndrome is present
Ophthalmological surveillance and low-vision support for chorioretinal dystrophy
Surveillance for emerging cerebellar ataxia and endocrine features across the PNPLA6 allelic spectrum
Genetic counselling for autosomal recessive inheritance with carrier testing of at-risk relatives
Multidisciplinary neurology, endocrinology, ophthalmology and rehabilitation input
